questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: What translation machines can and can't do
How to write a good letter to a friend in Spanish
Why airlines should always use human translators
How poets choose the best words for their poems
questions.why: Rob says they'll find out exactly what machines can and can't translate.

questions.q: How does Rob find the Spanish for 'it's raining'?
options: He remembers it from his Spanish lessons
He looks it up in a paper dictionary
He scans it with an app on his phone
He phones a friend who lives in Spain
questions.why: Rob says he has a new app: he holds up his phone and scans the word.

questions.q: What was the problem with older, rules-based translation software?
options: It could only translate between two languages
It had trouble with metaphors
It was too expensive for most people to use
It couldn't translate even simple words
questions.why: Rob says it worked fine for simple phrases, but not for more complex language like metaphors.

questions.q: According to Lane Greene, how does Google translate 'raining cats and dogs' into Spanish?
options: It translates each word one by one
It leaves the phrase in English
It asks the user to explain what they mean
It uses a matching Spanish idiom
questions.why: He says someone at Google input the Spanish phrase, so the whole chunk is translated into the equivalent metaphor.

questions.q: What is Michael Rosen trying to argue?
options: New poetry is too hard for machines
Machines will soon write better poems than people
Poets should use translation apps more often
Poetry is easier to translate than everyday speech
questions.why: He says he is 'sticking up for poetry' and trying to claim it's untranslatable for machines.

questions.q: According to Lane Greene, what advantage do humans have over machines?
options: Humans can memorise more words than machines
Humans can work much faster than computers
Humans can be new and creative
Humans never make any translation mistakes
questions.why: He says, 'our advantage is novelty and creativity'.

questions.q: What does Sam say machines really do when they 'learn' a language?
options: They understand the meaning like humans do
They study grammar books written by teachers
They talk to native speakers of each language
They find patterns in millions of translations
questions.why: Sam says they have been trained to identify patterns in millions and millions of translations.

questions.q: Why does Sam call the limits of machines 'good news' for her and Rob?
options: Because they don't like using technology
Their jobs using languages are safer
Because they can now write their own apps
Because they want to become poets
questions.why: She says it's good news for humans who use different languages in their jobs – 'like us!'
